title: Adaptive learning finds higher-activity Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction catalysts
summary: An adaptive-learning design-of-experiments loop guided robotic high-throughput synthesis of Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction electrocatalysts across a six-dimensional process/composition space. Starting from 36 characterized samples, the team synthesized 14 additional catalyst formulations from a nominal search space of roughly 10 billion combinations. Four outperformed the best sample in the initial dataset; the best showed about 33% higher ORR activity, reported as 16.3 mA mg⁻¹ at 0.8 V in rotating-disk measurements.
ai_technology: Adaptive learning framework with machine-learning surrogates, statistical inference, uncertainty quantification, and global optimization, paired with robotic high-throughput synthesis
organization: Los Alamos National Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory

evidence.tested: An adaptive-learning design-of-experiments loop guided robotic high-throughput synthesis of Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction electrocatalysts across a six-dimensional process/composition space.
evidence.unknown: The finding concerns optimized Fe–N–C catalyst formulations and synthesis conditions within the study’s defined six-dimensional search; it is not discovery of a new catalyst family or proof that all approximately 10 billion combinations were tested. The 33% improvement is relative to the best sample in the initial 36-sample dataset. Activity was measured using rotating-ring disk electrode testing, not a fuel-cell device or long-duration operating demonstration. The study reports 14 new synthesized catalysts and four that beat the initial samples; these are one paper-level result, not separate entries.
evidence.ai_role: The model-based design-of-experiments tool used current measurements and uncertainty to select subsequent synthesis conditions in a six-dimensional search space. It guided the selection of 14 samples for synthesis and measurement, producing four catalysts that exceeded the initial best. Robotic high-throughput synthesis and RRDE testing generated the experimental feedback; researchers interpreted the results.
